title: fix(tags-picker): keep search results visible after selecting a suggestion
body:
## Description

When the user taps a hashtag suggestion in the video metadata tags picker, the search field is now cleared so the next query can start fresh, but the existing query string and suggestion list are preserved. This lets the user rapidly pick several related tags in a row instead of retyping the search after every selection.

Previously, `_addTag` dispatched `TagsPickerSearchReset`, which wiped the bloc's `query` and `suggestions`. The new behaviour swaps the controller value while the `_onSearchChanged` listener is temporarily detached, so no `TagsPickerQueryChanged('')` fires and the bloc's query/suggestions stay intact.

Additional cleanups in the same change:

- Wrap the `_TagChip` label in `Flexible` with `maxLines: 1` + ellipsis so long tag names don't overflow the chip.
- Drop the now-unused `TagsPickerSearchReset` event, its `on<...>` registration, and the `_onSearchReset` handler.
- Update the widget test to assert that the previous query (`mus`) remains visible after tapping a suggestion.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4641

## Out of Scope

None.

title: feat(dm): emoji reactions on messages (#4633)
body:
Closes #4633.

## Summary

Lets a Divine user react to a DM message with an emoji. Reactions ride
the same NIP-17 seal + gift-wrap envelope as the underlying DM (NIP-17
spec line 14 explicitly allows kind-7 reactions inside the encrypted
chat), so privacy is reuse-of-spec rather than custom design.

- 6-emoji quick row + `+` entry, shown above the existing Copy / Delete
  / Report actions in a single long-press overlay.
- Compact bordered chip beneath the bubble, overlapping its bottom
  corner. Own / theirs / pending / failed variants.
- Cap one reaction per user per message in v1; supersede on a
  different emoji emits NIP-09 kind-5 deletion of the prior.
- Hidden on failed-send own DMs.

## Architecture

UI → BLoC → Repository → Client, per `architecture.md`.

| Layer | Files |
|---|---|
| Client | None — reuses `NIP17MessageService.buildRumor(eventKind: 7)` + `sendRumor` unchanged. |
| Repository | `dm_repository` extended with `DmReactionsRepository` + reportable-sites constants; new branch at `_handleGiftWrapEvent` line 511 routes `rumor.kind == 7` to the new repo before the existing 14/15 gate. |
| BLoC | `lib/blocs/dm/reactions/` — cubit with restartable/sequential transformers and addError-without-Reportable per the matrix. |
| Persistence | `DmMessageReactions` Drift table (dedup on `(id, owner_pubkey)`, partial indexes, soft-delete + rumor JSON columns) + `DmReactionsDao` (insertOptimistic / swapPlaceholderId / markPending / markFailed / softDelete / upsertIncoming / watchForConversation). |
| Widgets | `ReactionChip` in `divine_ui` (strict-coverage tests included); `ReactionsRow` + `ReactionPickerOverlay` in the feature folder. |
| l10n | 11 new `dmReaction*` keys in `app_en.arb`, added to `_knownUntranslatedDebt` (matches #4631 markdown precedent). |

## Reliability hardening

The user reproduced a retry-doesn't-work scenario: a failed reaction
could not be retried by tapping, but a single retry tap after
hot-restart succeeded. Three compounding bugs caused it:

1. **No timeout on `sendRumor`** — a stalled relay socket left the
   awaited future hanging indefinitely; the `sequential()` event
   transformer queued every subsequent retry behind the hung one.
   **Fix:** wrap `sendRumor` in a 15 s timeout
   (`_sendRumorWithTimeout` in the repository, applied to both
   `publish` and `retry`). Timeouts surface as `NIP17SendFailure`.
2. **No DAO-persisted in-flight state** — the cubit's in-memory
   `pending` map was the only signal of a retry in progress; a cubit
   rebuild (auth flip, navigation, hot-restart) lost it and the chip
   reverted to the stale persisted state. **Fix:** new
   `DmReactionsDao.markPending` writes `publishStatus = 'pending'`
   to the row before the send. On any non-success outcome (timeout,
   failure, throw) the row flips back to `'failed'`, so the chip is
   tappable again immediately.
3. **`BlocSelector` missed pending-map updates** — the row selector
   was keyed only on `state.reactionsFor(messageId)`, so transitions
   in `state.pending` did not rebuild the chip and the captured
   `agg.isFailed` could be stale. **Fix:** swap to `BlocBuilder`
   with a per-message `buildWhen` that includes both the reactions
   list and this message's pending entries. Also added a guard at
   the top of `_onTap` to drop taps on pending chips so a tap during
   retry can't fall through to the toggle branch and silently delete
   the in-flight reaction.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean (32.5s).
- [x] `divine_ui` package tests: 585 / 585 (includes 9 new chip tests).
- [x] `dm_repository` package tests: 240 / 240 (no regression from the
      kind-7 routing branch + new constructor parameter).
- [x] `db_client` package tests: 616 / 616 (the new table is additive).
- [x] `ConversationView` widget tests: 33 / 33 (the existing pump
      helper now provides a mock `ConversationReactionsCubit`).
- [x] `ConversationReactionsCubit` blocTest cases: 4 / 4.
- [x] `arb_consistency_test.dart` passes with the 11 new keys added
      to `_knownUntranslatedDebt`.

### Manual reproduction of the retry hardening

1. Send a DM to a peer.
2. Disconnect the device from the network OR force-stop the configured
   DM relays so the next publish hangs.
3. Long-press your sent bubble → tap any emoji from the quick row.
4. **Before this PR:** chip flips to failed; tapping it does nothing
   until the app is hot-restarted.
5. **After this PR:** chip flips to pending while the send is
   in-flight; within ≤ 15 s it falls back to failed; tapping it again
   actually re-attempts; multiple rapid taps are dropped while pending
   so the optimistic state cannot be silently destroyed.

### Manual reproduction of the happy path

1. Open a DM conversation.
2. Long-press any bubble → quick-row picker overlays the action sheet.
3. Tap ❤️ → chip appears on the bubble's bottom corner immediately
   (optimistic), persists across app restart, and lands on the peer
   via the existing NIP-17 pipeline.
4. Long-press the same bubble → tap a different emoji → the prior
   chip disappears (cap-at-one supersede via kind-5 deletion) and
   the new one appears.

## Out of scope for v1

Tracked separately as follow-up issues:

- Full `emoji_picker_flutter` wiring for the `+` entry.
- Group-DM reaction routing (1:1 only at v1).
- Reaction notifications (encrypted variant — needs its own privacy spec).
- Multi-react per message (drop the cap-at-one).
- Full ARB translation for the 16 non-English locales.
- Reaction detail sheet (only useful once groups land).

## Notes

- Brainstorm doc covering the 60-round design exploration lives
  locally at
  `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-23-issue4633-dm-emoji-reactions-brainstorm.md`
  and is intentionally not committed.
- Draft because (a) optional design check on the quick-row emoji set
  ❤️ 😂 🔥 😮 😢 👍 before merge, and (b) manual repro of the retry
  hardening on a real device is recommended before flipping to ready.

title: feat(dm): emoji reactions on messages

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Summary

Let users react to a DM message with an emoji, the way they can in iMessage, WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram, and Discord. Today there is no react affordance on a DM bubble — the long-press sheet on `message_actions_sheet.dart` only exposes Copy / Copy video URL / Delete / Report. Users coming from any other messenger find the absence jarring.

## How would this be useful?

Reactions are the lowest-friction way to acknowledge a message — a thumbs up on a plan, a heart on a photo, a laugh on a joke. Without them, the only way to respond is to type a reply, which is heavier and clutters the thread.

## Proposed scope (initial)

- Long-press on any DM bubble → quick reaction row (5–6 default emojis, e.g. ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🙏 🫶 — final set TBD with design) plus a "+" entry into a full picker.
- Tapping a reaction toggles it (tap again to un-react). One reaction per user per message at first; multi-react can land later.
- Reactions render as a small chip beneath the bubble showing emoji + count, with own reactions highlighted.
- Tapping the chip shows who reacted with what (1:1 DM means just the other party, but the affordance should work for future group DMs).
- Sent and received bubbles behave identically.

Out of scope for the first pass:
- Custom / animated reactions
- Reaction notifications (separate decision — see Notes)
- Group DM reactions (no group DMs yet)

## Privacy considerations

This is the interesting part — we are trying to maximize privacy within the constraints of what we have.

We already ship NIP-25 reactions (kind 7) for videos and comments via `mobile/packages/likes_repository/`. **Reusing that primitive verbatim for DMs would leak metadata**: a plaintext kind-7 event tagged with the encrypted DM's id would publicly announce "user A reacted to event B" even though B is a NIP-17 gift-wrapped DM that should not be linkable to either party.

The reaction must be wrapped the same way the underlying DM is:

- DM messages are kind 14 (chat message) sealed (kind 13) and gift-wrapped (kind 1059) per NIP-17.
- A reaction needs the same envelope: a kind-7 (or DM-scoped reaction kind — open question) sealed and gift-wrapped to the recipient(s). The outer 1059 must not reveal which message is being reacted to.
- The inner reaction event references the DM's id via an `e` tag, which is only visible after unwrap.
- Both participants need a copy (sender wraps to self + recipient, mirroring how outgoing DMs are stored — see `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation/` and `mobile/packages/dm_repository/`).

Open spec questions to resolve before implementation:
- [ ] Reuse kind 7 inside the seal, or define a DM-specific reaction kind? (Reuse keeps interop with other NIP-17 clients that might already do this; a new kind avoids ambiguity.)
- [ ] How does the recipient enumerate reactions for a given DM? The seal carries `["e", <dm-id>]`, but the DM id itself is only known after unwrap of the original message — we need a join on already-unwrapped events client-side.
- [ ] Storage: extend the existing DM tables (`outgoing_dms`, conversation cache) with a reactions side-table keyed by `(conversation_id, message_id, reactor_pubkey)`, or denormalize onto the message row.
- [ ] Send reliability: reactions should ride the same retry / self-wrap recovery path as DMs (see #4106, #4241, #4410) — a half-delivered reaction is worse than no reaction.
- [ ] Notifications: react-to-DM notifications would themselves need to be encrypted, which is a deeper decision. Out of scope for v1 — start with in-app only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Long-pressing a DM bubble surfaces a reactions row above the existing actions sheet.
- [ ] Tapping a reaction publishes a wrapped reaction event to both self and recipient and optimistically renders the chip.
- [ ] Tapping the same reaction again removes it (publishes a NIP-09 deletion of the reaction).
- [ ] Reaction chip renders under the message bubble with emoji + count; own reaction is visually distinct.
- [ ] Reactions persist across app restarts (stored locally, not re-fetched on every cold start).
- [ ] Reactions survive the same failure modes DMs do: self-wrap-only recovery, recipient-failed sweeps, etc.
- [ ] Reactions are NOT discoverable on public relays as "X reacted to a DM" — only the involved pubkeys can decrypt.
- [ ] Works for both NIP-17 DMs and the legacy NIP-04 path if both are still live in production at ship time.

## Notes

- Related: #4620 (DM multi-line input), #4621 (DM markdown formatting — merged via #4631). This sits alongside those as the next DM UX gap.
- Prior art in this repo: existing NIP-25 plumbing in `mobile/packages/likes_repository/`, NIP-17 send/receive flow in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/`, retry infrastructure in `mobile/lib/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service.dart`. Reuse the retry primitive, do NOT reuse `likes_repository` unmodified — the privacy envelope is the whole point.
- A short design doc / brainstorm under `mobile/docs/brainstorm/` should land before implementation kicks off, given the spec questions above.

title: fix(feed): stop native feed playback when home is inactive
body:
## Summary

Closes #4640.

This fixes a regression in the native home-feed player path where feed audio could continue playing after the home feed became inactive, especially when opening the recorder while the active video was still initializing.

## Problem

The native `InfiniteVideoFeed` implementation only exposed imperative `pauseActive()` / `resumeActive()` methods. It did not have a durable internal playback-active state.

That meant async code paths inside the package could still call `play()` after the feed had already been paused:

- initial controller init completion
- page changes
- source failover

In the recorder repro from #4640, the home feed could be paused while the controller was still loading, then the async init would complete and unconditionally restart playback underneath the recorder.

The package also treated pause as only a direct controller pause. It did not stop the active watchdog and stale-playback detector when the feed became inactive.

## What changed

### `InfiniteVideoFeed`

- Added a declarative `isActive` input, defaulting to `true`.
- Introduced internal `_isActive` state so playback eligibility survives async work.
- Centralized active/inactive transitions:
  - inactive pauses the current controller when ready
  - inactive stops the load watchdog
  - inactive stops stale playback detection
  - active resumes the current ready controller and restarts watchdog/detector
- Gated all internal autoplay paths on `_isActive`:
  - controller init completion
  - page changes
  - source failover
- Kept `pauseActive()` / `resumeActive()` as public API, but made them thin wrappers over the same source of truth.

### `FeedVideos`

- Removed the imperative `didUpdateWidget` pause/resume side channel.
- Passed a declarative `isActive` flag into `InfiniteVideoFeed`.
- Combined parent activity with `RouteAware` visibility into one effective feed-active boolean.
- Kept route-aware pause/resume behavior for pushed routes, but now via declarative state instead of direct player pokes.

## Tests

Added race-focused coverage for the native player path:

- no autoplay when the feed mounts inactive
- no autoplay when the feed becomes inactive during controller init
- no autoplay on page change while inactive
- no autoplay on source failover while inactive
- playback resumes when the current controller becomes active again
- `FeedVideos` propagates effective activity into `InfiniteVideoFeed`
- route-aware callbacks toggle that activity state correctly

## Verification

Ran locally:

- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test`
- `flutter test packages/infinite_video_feed`
- `flutter test test/widgets/video_feed_item`
- `flutter test test/screens/feed`

These also re-ran as part of the branch push hook for the changed files.

title: fix(video): recover collaborator invites from outgoing dm queue
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4636 by making collaborator invite recovery queue-backed and durable instead of relying on a one-shot snackbar retry after publish.

Before this change, a successful video publish could still leave collaborator invites unsent. Those failures were surfaced only through a short-lived snackbar, and the manual retry path minted a brand new invite DM instead of recovering the original queued send. That meant users could easily miss the retry affordance, and any future persistent retry UI would risk duplicate invites if the original queued DM later recovered.

This PR changes the recovery model to use the existing `outgoing_dms` queue as the single source of truth.

## Root Cause

The issue was not that collaborator invites had no persistence. They were already enqueued in `outgoing_dms` before publish. The real gaps were:

- successful video publish treated collaborator invite delivery as best-effort
- failure feedback was ephemeral and easy to miss
- manual retry re-sent a fresh collaborator invite instead of recovering the queued rumor
- diagnostics were not specific enough to distinguish video publish failures from collaborator invite delivery failures

## What Changed

### Queue-backed collaborator invite recovery

- Added `CollaboratorInviteRecoveryService` to parse collaborator invite rows from `outgoing_dms`
- Grouped unresolved invites by video address for author-facing recovery
- Retried by calling `DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId: ...)` on the original queued row
- Filtered the persistent banner to recipient-delivery failures so self-wrap-only recovery does not create false author-facing alarms

### Persistent author-side recovery UI

- Added Riverpod providers to expose the recovery service and pending invite groups
- Added a persistent inline banner on the author's own profile video grid for videos with unresolved collaborator invite delivery
- Wired banner retry to queue recovery instead of creating a new invite message
- Updated the publish snackbar retry button to use the same queue-backed recovery path

### Diagnostics and cleanup

- Enriched collaborator invite failure logging in `VideoPublishService` with video address, creator pubkey, and per-invite failure details
- Enriched NIP-17 send failure logging with rumor id and recipient pubkey
- Enriched video event publish logging with configured and connected relay counts plus failure reason when available
- Removed the old duplicate-prone `retryCollaboratorInvite()` resend path so there is one retry mechanism instead of two

## Why This Is Safer

- The retry path now recovers the original queued send instead of minting a second collaborator invite rumor
- The UI is driven from durable queue state, so it survives navigation and app restarts
- Auto-retry and manual retry now operate on the same underlying queue record rather than competing mechanisms
- The author-facing banner only appears for unresolved recipient delivery, which is the user-visible failure mode

## Tests

### Local verification run

- `flutter test test/services/collaborator_invite_recovery_service_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/widgets/profile/profile_videos_grid_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/services/video_publish/video_publish_service_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/src/nip17_message_service_test.dart` from `mobile/packages/dm_repository`
- targeted `flutter analyze` on all touched app and test files
- repo pre-push checks passed, including changed-file analyze and changed-file test selection

### Added coverage

- recovery service only surfaces unresolved collaborator invite rows
- retry only recovers matching queued rows for the selected video and collaborators
- partial retry failures are reported correctly
- own-profile banner rendering and gating
- banner retry uses queue-backed recovery

## Review Notes

The most important behavior change is that collaborator invite retry is no longer a resend operation. It is now a recovery operation over the original `outgoing_dms` record, which avoids duplicate collaborator DMs and gives us a durable source of truth for pending invite state.

title: fix(profile): render svg avatars without codec warnings
body:
## Summary
- render SVG avatar URLs through `SvgPicture.network` instead of raster decoding them through `VineCachedImage`
- keep the existing placeholder path for load failures and invalid avatar data
- add regression coverage for SVG URL classification and non-network avatar rendering branches

## Root Cause
Avatar URLs were always routed through the raster image cache path. When profile metadata or upstream defaults supplied an `.svg` URL, Flutter attempted bitmap decoding, logged codec warnings, and rebuilt the placeholder repeatedly.

- add `UserAvatar.isSvgImageUrl(...)` so SVG URL detection is explicit and regression-tested
- branch SVG network avatars to `SvgPicture.network` with the same placeholder safety net
- keep raster URLs on `VineCachedImage` and keep direct `imageProvider` inputs on the existing local image path

## Safety
- raster avatar behavior is unchanged
- invalid or failed SVG loads still fall back to the existing placeholder
- the regression tests avoid brittle network mocking and cover the branch selection logic directly

title: fix(feed): cancel video feed subscriptions on close
body:
## Summary
- replace `emit.onEach` startup listeners in `VideoFeedBloc` with explicitly owned `StreamSubscription`s
- cancel feed subscriptions during bloc shutdown and guard internal `add(...)` calls after close
- extend the bloc regression test to prove both listeners are torn down before post-close stream emissions

## Root Cause
`VideoFeedStarted` installed long-lived stream listeners without owning their lifecycle in `close()`. During navigation away from Home, a late follow or curated-list emission could still call `add(...)` after bloc shutdown and throw `Bad state: Cannot add new events after calling close`.

## Changes
- store startup subscriptions for `followingStream` and `subscribedListsStream` on the bloc
- cancel and clear those subscriptions in `close()` before delegating to `super.close()`
- use a small `_addIfOpen(...)` guard for any callback racing with shutdown
- keep the existing first-following-emission dedupe behavior intact

## Safety
- no feed selection or fetch behavior changed outside shutdown handling
- subscriptions are still created only after the initial load completes
- tests now verify both listener cleanup and post-close stream safety

## Validation
- `flutter analyze lib/blocs/video_feed/video_feed_bloc.dart test/blocs/video_feed/video_feed_bloc_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/blocs/video_feed/video_feed_bloc_test.dart`
- pre-push changed-file analyzer and test gates

Fixes #4644

title: fix(feed): guard VideoFeedBloc stream callbacks after close
body:
## Summary

`VideoFeedBloc` subscribes to long-lived repository streams in `_onStarted` and can still `add(...)` events after the bloc has been disposed. This shows up in production logs as `Bad state: Cannot add new events after calling close` during navigation away from feed surfaces.

## Evidence

Observed in local log capture `openvine_full_logs_2026-05-22T19-36-42.547446.txt`:
- `Bloc error: VideoFeedBloc: Bad state: Cannot add new events after calling close`
- Stack begins `_BroadcastStreamController.add -> Bloc.add`

Current code path:
- `mobile/lib/blocs/video_feed/video_feed_bloc.dart`
- `_onStarted()` calls `emit.onEach(_followRepository.followingStream, onData: ... add(VideoFeedFollowingListChanged(...)))`
- `_onStarted()` also awaits `emit.onEach(_curatedListRepository.subscribedListsStream.skip(1), onData: ... add(VideoFeedCuratedListsChanged(...)))`
- The bloc does not own/cancel those subscriptions explicitly in `close()` and does not guard `add(...)` with `isClosed`.

## Impact

- Noisy bloc errors in logs during normal navigation
- Real lifecycle bug that can mask other feed teardown problems
- Same bug class as other existing `add after close` / `emit after close` fixes, but in a high-churn feed path

## Scope

- Make `VideoFeedBloc` own and dispose its stream subscriptions explicitly
- Prevent repository stream callbacks from calling `add(...)` after close
- Keep behavior identical while mounted; this is a lifecycle hardening fix, not a feed-behavior refactor
- Add focused tests that close the bloc before follow/curated-list streams emit and assert no state error occurs

## Acceptance criteria

- `VideoFeedBloc` does not throw `Cannot add new events after calling close` when the page is disposed while upstream streams still emit
- Follow-list and curated-list refresh behavior remains unchanged while the bloc is alive
- Regression tests cover both stream sources
- `flutter analyze` and affected feed tests pass

## Related

- Similar bug class: #4393
- Reliability epic: #4336

title: fix(video): fail over on critical ready-state playback errors
body:
## Summary
- treat classified 401/403/404 ready-state playback errors as real source failures in `VideoFeedController`

## Summary

`VideoFeedController` can get stuck in a broken fallback state when a Divine-hosted progressive source fails, a fallback source opens, and later playback errors arrive after the controller has already transitioned to `LoadState.ready`.

- progressive source fails: `/720p.mp4`
- controller logs `stuck_failover` and retries the raw blob URL

- Reproduce the failing sequence with controller-level tests
- Allow the controller to continue fallback recovery or terminate cleanly when a selected fallback source later proves unusable
- Avoid infinite retries and avoid regressing legitimate transient ready-state player events

- A video that fails on progressive and later fails on raw/HLS does not loop indefinitely

title: fix(notifications): guard owned-video notification attribution
body:
## Summary
- validate referenced video ownership before rendering first-party video notifications
- drop misattributed video-like notifications when the fetched video owner is known not to match the signed-in user
- stop forging NIP-33 video routes for actor-anchored comment notifications when the payload does not carry authoritative owner metadata
- add regression coverage for paged fetch, realtime enrichment, and snapshot insertion paths

## Root Cause
The notification repository treated any reaction with a referenced video as a like on the current user's video and synthesized `34236:<current-user-pubkey>:<d-tag>` routes from that assumption. When the backend returned a notification tied to a video owned by someone else, the client rendered a false "liked your video" row and built the wrong destination.

## What Changed
- gate video-anchored notification grouping and realtime enrichment on known video ownership
- build stable video addressable IDs from the referenced video's owner pubkey instead of the signed-in user's pubkey
- suppress actor-anchored stable route synthesis until the API includes authoritative owner metadata for the parent video
- log dropped misattributed notifications with enough context to debug backend payload attribution

## Safety
- only suppresses notifications when the owner mismatch is positively known from fetched video stats
- keeps existing behavior when ownership metadata is absent, so the change is narrowly scoped to the proven bad path
- leaves actor-anchored notifications resolver-based instead of sending users to a forged stable route
- adds tests for both valid owned-video notifications and rejected foreign-video notifications

title: fix(notifications): reject misattributed video-like notifications for non-owned videos
body:
## Summary
A notification can currently render as 'liked your video' even when the liked video is not owned by the signed-in user.

This is user-visible, misleading, and affects both notification copy and notification tap routing.

Parent: #4200

## Evidence
Log: /Users/lizsw/openvine_full_logs_2026-05-22T21-32-35.355036.txt

Relevant line:
- 1116: NotificationsView navigates from the notification using addressable=34236:0edc2f474484769bc9bf6d471d180e4e280b0bcd719b6da791001beb730cff1b:364cc91e57385573a4e0b8b7a26f75c3747a4242a6e7f8c3a82aab8b7c9a7606 eventId=4093b21a1805f78c56d8c2f23386e9ace4a7b615849afacd871618066585a577.

The client synthesized a NIP-33 route using the signed-in users pubkey as the video owner component. That is only valid if the referenced video actually belongs to the signed-in user.

## Current Likely Failure Mode
- Funnelcake returns a reaction notification with referenced_video populated.
- NotificationRepository maps that directly to NotificationKind.like based on isReferencedVideo.
- The repository then builds the addressable ID as 34236:<current-user-pubkey>:<d-tag>.
- The UI renders liked your video and navigates as if ownership were confirmed.
- In this case, the underlying liked video appears to belong to someone else.

## Why This Is A Bug
The client is inferring ownership from notification shape instead of validating ownership from the referenced video metadata.

That means a bad or over-broad notification payload can become a false first-party notification in the UI.

## Suspected Root Cause
This is likely split across two layers:

### Client
NotificationRepository assumes all video-anchored notifications are about the current users content when synthesizing videoAddressableId.

### Backend
The notifications API may be sending a reaction notification to a user whose video was not actually the liked target, possibly in reply-video or thread-related cases.

## Correct Fix Direction
### Client hardening
- Validate referenced video ownership before rendering a video-anchored your-video notification.
- Use VideoStats.pubkey when available.
- Do not synthesize 34236:<current-user-pubkey>:<d-tag> unless the referenced video owner matches the signed-in user.
- If ownership cannot be validated or does not match, drop or safely downgrade the notification instead of lying.

### Backend follow-up
- Verify why /api/users/:pubkey/notifications emitted this notification.
- Confirm whether reply-video or thread-context reactions are being misattributed to the wrong recipient.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A reaction on another users video never renders as liked your video for the signed-in user.
- Notification tap routing never synthesizes a current-user-owned video addressable ID unless ownership is confirmed.
- Regression coverage exists for a referenced_video notification whose referenced video owner does not match the signed-in user.
- Backend tracking exists if the API payload is confirmed to be wrong.

## Notes
Related context:
- #4200 notifications stabilization epic
- #4202 video replies context may be relevant if this originated from reply-video or thread behavior

title: fix(invite): guard invite status lifecycle and auth gating
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4393.

This hardens `InviteStatusCubit` against the two failure modes currently showing up around invite-status loads:
- async completion after the cubit has already been closed
- expected cold-start auth gaps that briefly make invite requests unauthenticated and return `401 auth_required`

## Root cause

`InviteStatusCubit.load()` and `generateInvite()` emitted state unconditionally after awaited network work completed. If the settings surface or app shell disposed the cubit first, Bloc would raise an `emit after close` error.

Separately, invite-status loads could run before NIP-98 auth was ready to mint headers on cold start or resume. That produced a transient `401` from the invite service, which the cubit treated as a generic failure even though the underlying app session had not actually failed.

## What changed

- Added an `isInviteAuthReady` gate to `InviteStatusCubit` and wired it from `nip98AuthServiceProvider.canCreateTokens` in `main.dart`.
- Prevented invite-status requests from starting while invite auth is not ready.
- Restored the previous invite state instead of surfacing a generic error when the invite API returns the expected `401 auth_required` gap.
- Added `_emitIfOpen(...)` so late async completions do not emit after the cubit has been closed.
- Added focused tests for:
  - auth-not-ready no-op behavior
  - `401 auth_required` rollback to previous state
  - close-before-completion lifecycle safety

## Why this is safe

- The change is local to the invite cubit boundary and its provider wiring.
- Successful invite fetch and invite generation paths are unchanged.
- Unexpected failures still flow through `addError(...)` and the existing error state.
- The new auth gate only blocks invite calls when the app cannot currently create the required NIP-98 header.

## Validation

Local:
- `flutter test test/blocs/invite_status/invite_status_cubit_test.dart`
- `flutter analyze lib/blocs/invite_status/invite_status_cubit.dart lib/main.dart test/blocs/invite_status/invite_status_cubit_test.dart`

title: fix: saved edits and account data disappear after reopening app
body:
## Summary

Saved edits and other local app data could disappear after reopening the app.
The confirmed bug was in native SQLite startup, not in the auth session cleanup path.
This change stops stale database version handling from deleting the active database and makes legacy database recovery preserve user data instead of guessing which database should win.

**Related Issue:** Part of #4577

## What Changed

The app now treats the local SQLite database as user data, not disposable cache.
It preserves the current database during version adoption and handles the old Documents-to-Application-Support path move safely.

- Preserve the current Application Support database when the stored database version is stale.
- Restore the legacy Documents database when the current destination is empty or only contains replaceable/cache state.
- Classify actionable local-only rows before deciding whether a destination database owns user data.
- Back up cache-only destination files and SQLite sidecars before restoring legacy data.
- When both databases contain active local rows, keep the current database active and move the legacy database beside it as a conflict backup.
- Move `sqlite3` to package dependencies because production startup code now reads SQLite metadata directly.

## Background

The two database locations come from a previous app-data path move.
PR #2840 changed the SQLite path from Documents to Application Support while fixing notifications; that location is defensible for hidden app data, but it originally shipped without a migration.
PR #2887 then added a one-time migration from the legacy Documents database to the new Application Support database.

This PR handles the cases left after that history.
Some users can have a stale version marker, an empty or cache-only destination database, or both a legacy database and a current database with local rows.
Those cases need data-preserving startup behavior instead of deleting, clobbering, or silently orphaning one database.

## Not Auth-Related

The original report mentioned account data and following state, so I checked that path separately.
The reproducible failure we found was SQLite data loss on app startup; same-user auth restore and the SharedPreferences following cache did not reproduce as the cause.

- This does not change OAuth session restore.
- This does not change `following_list_<pubkey>` SharedPreferences cache behavior.
- Focused follow/reopen E2E coverage is split into #4639.

## Testing

I tested the native database startup path directly and also verified the CI failure that appeared after the final review fix.
The regression tests cover stale version adoption, legacy restore over empty and cache-only destinations, actionable queue-row classification, sidecar backup, populated destination preservation, conflict backup, and WAL/SHM migration.

- `flutter analyze lib test` from `mobile/packages/db_client`
- `flutter test test/src/database/connection/connection_native_test.dart` from `mobile/packages/db_client`
- `mise exec -- flutter analyze lib test integration_test` from `mobile`

## Risks

The main risk is the conflicted two-database case.
This change preserves both databases there, but it does not merge rows automatically because drafts, pending actions, reactions, reposts, and direct messages can conflict.

- Current behavior: keep the current database active and save the legacy database as a conflict backup.
- Remaining work: add a deliberate reconciliation flow if we want to merge or surface those conflicts in the app.

title: refactor(comments): split comments_bloc.dart into three focused blocs
body:
## Description

Carves the 1,462-line `CommentsBloc` into three focused successor blocs composed via `MultiBlocProvider`, with cross-bloc coordination going through `BlocListener`-bridged outbox signals per `.claude/rules/state_management.md`'s no-BLoC-to-BLoC dependency rule.

### Successor blocs (each under 500 lines)

| Bloc | Lines | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `CommentsListBloc` | **497** | Canonical `commentsById` store, load / paginate / sort / real-time stream / EOSE tracking, plus six new store-mutation events received from the two other blocs' outbox signals (`OptimisticCommentInserted`/`Confirmed`/`RolledBack`, `CommentReplacedInStore`, `CommentRemovedFromStore`, `CommentsRemovedByAuthorFromStore`). |
| `CommentComposerBloc` | **498** | Main / reply / edit input state, two-tier mention search (`restartable()`), publish + edit publish flows; emits `ComposerOutbox{Insert,Confirm,Rollback}Placeholder` / `ReplaceComment` for the UI to bridge into list-bloc store mutations. |
| `CommentReactionsBloc` | **388** | Vote / vote-counts fetch / report / block / delete with `droppable()` transformers; emits `ReactionsOutbox{RemoveComment,RemoveByAuthor}` for list cleanup after block + delete. |

### Outbox bridging

`_OutboxBridges` in `comments_screen.dart` wires two `BlocListener`s that translate composer / reactions outbox state changes into `CommentsListBloc` events, then dispatches `ComposerOutboxConsumed` / `ReactionsOutboxConsumed` to clear the signal. The bridge also re-dispatches `CommentVoteCountsFetchRequested` onto `CommentReactionsBloc` whenever the loaded comment set changes (replaces the previous self-add inside `CommentsBloc._onLoadRequested`).

### Helper extractions (pure-Dart, no bloc dependency)

To keep each bloc under the issue's 500-line acceptance criterion:

- `comments_list/throttled_subscription.dart` — token-bucket stream listener + auto-cancelling subscription wrapper.
- `comments_list/comments_list_helpers.dart` — `commentEngagementScore` + `computeReplyCounts`.
- `comment_composer/mention_search.dart` — tier-1 local + tier-2 REST mention search returning plain records so the bloc owns the user-facing `MentionSuggestion` type.

### #4478 cache-key fix preserved

`rootAddressableId` is injected into all three blocs at construction. Every `postComment` / `deleteComment` / `loadComments` call site verifies the addressable-id thread-through via `verify()` (three explicit "(#4478)" tests in the new bloc test files). Three new outbox-emission tests guard the optimistic-placeholder reconciliation including the relay-echo-arrives-first race that `_onNewCommentReceived` resolves by matching placeholder by author+content.

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [x] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Verification

- `flutter test test/blocs/comments/ test/screens/comments/` — **133/133 pass**, including 17 reactions tests, 20 composer tests, 24 list-bloc tests, and 72 widget tests covering the new `MultiBlocProvider` tree.
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — **0 issues**.
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed lib/blocs/comments/ lib/screens/comments/ test/blocs/comments/ test/screens/comments/` — clean.
- `wc -l` each successor bloc:
  - `comments_list_bloc.dart` — 497 lines
  - `comment_composer_bloc.dart` — 498 lines
  - `comment_reactions_bloc.dart` — 388 lines

## Manual test plan

- [ ] Open comments sheet on a NIP-71 addressable video → list loads.
- [ ] Type and send a comment → placeholder appears immediately; settles to real id on relay echo.
- [ ] Edit own comment → original removed and replacement appears in-place.
- [ ] Delete own comment → row disappears.
- [ ] Block another user → all their comments disappear from the open sheet.
- [ ] Upvote / downvote / switch / remove vote → net score updates optimistically, reverts on relay failure.
- [ ] Report a comment → no list mutation, no error toast.
- [ ] Cycle sort modes (New → Top → Old → New) → engagement sort reads upvote counts from reactions bloc through `comments_list.dart`'s nested `BlocSelector`.
- [ ] Edit a video that has ≥1 comment → re-open from profile → comment count does not drop to 0 (preserves #4478 cache fix).

## Acceptance criteria (from #4516)

- [x] Each successor bloc is under 500 lines. (497 / 498 / 388)
- [x] Existing comment widget tests pass after the split (provider-tree updated to `MultiBlocProvider`).
- [x] Cache-key fix from #4478 (addressable-edit dedup) is preserved.

title: fix(security): remove BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth PKCE verifier and request body
body:
Source audit context: fresh `origin/main` worktree `.worktrees/audit-codebase-2026-04-24` at commit `33f6e026a`.
This issue was generated from the April 2026 codebase audit and includes file/line evidence from that snapshot.

## Severity
Critical

## Problem
BYOK registration embeds the user nsec into the PKCE verifier and posts the nsec to Keycast during headless registration.

## Evidence
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/pkce.dart:9-12 appends .$nsec to the PKCE verifier.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:155-171 accepts optional nsec and uses it in verifier generation.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:280-286 derives BYOK pubkey and generates verifier with nsec.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:299-301 puts nsec into the registration request body.
- mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart:81-95 exports local nsec and passes it into registration.
- mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart:117-122 calls headlessRegister(... nsec: nsec ...).

## Impact
BYOK/private key material leaves local storage and is also carried in the PKCE verifier, breaking the expected local-key custody boundary.

## Recommended fix
Never send or embed nsec. Use a local proof-of-possession challenge signed by the key, or send only byok_pubkey and a signature over server-provided nonce/session data.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No nsec appears in OAuth URL, PKCE verifier, persisted pending verification, request body, logs, or tests.
- [ ] Server receives only public key plus proof.
- [ ] BYOK registration still binds the account to the intended Nostr pubkey.
- [ ] Tests assert verifier does not contain nsec1.

## Related issues
Adjacent: #969, #3066, #3270.

title: fix(security): strip BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth wire (#3359)
body:
## Description

Phase 1 emergency block for #3359 — strips the user's nsec from the
Keycast OAuth registration wire on both channels:

- `body['nsec']` field in `POST /api/headless/register`
- `<random>.<nsec1...>` suffix embedded in the PKCE `code_verifier`
  (later POSTed as `code_verifier` to `/api/oauth/token`)

The fix removes the parameters from the `keycast_flutter` package API
entirely so a future caller cannot re-introduce the leak. A POSIX-grep
CI guard locks the rule in.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3359

**Cross-repo coordination:** divinevideo/keycast#197 tracks the
server-side proof-of-possession redesign that Phase 2 depends on.
This PR ships **without** preserving BYOK identity binding — that is
restored once Phase 2 lands.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ❌ Breaking change (the public `KeycastOAuth.headlessRegister` and `KeycastOAuth.getAuthorizationUrl` APIs no longer accept `nsec` — intentional, for security)

## Trade-off

Until Phase 2 ships, BYOK secure-account upgrades fall through to the
server's auto-generate path. The user's existing local pubkey identity
is **not preserved** across the upgrade, but the local nsec stays
on-device and never crosses the network. This is the intentional
emergency-block trade-off — stop the leak today, restore identity
preservation in Phase 2 (depends on divinevideo/keycast#197).

## What's in this PR

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/pkce.dart` | `generateVerifier` no longer takes `nsec`; verifier is always pure-random base64url |
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart` | `getAuthorizationUrl` & `headlessRegister` drop `nsec`/`byokPubkey` parameters; `body['nsec']` removed; `byok_pubkey` URL param removed |
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/test/{pkce,oauth_client}_test.dart` | Leak-as-feature tests flipped to negative regression guards |
| `mobile/lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart` | `load()` discards any persisted verifier containing `.nsec1` and clears storage (defense-in-depth migration) |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit.dart` | Error log no longer interpolates `_pendingVerifier` value |
| `mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart` | Removed `authService.exportNsec()` and the `nsec:` arg |
| `mobile/test/services/pending_verification_service_test.dart` | **New** — three tests for the migration |
| `mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` | **New** — POSIX-grep guard for production code |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` | New `nsec-leak-guard` job |
| `mobile/integration_test/auth/session_expired_banner_test.dart` | `markTestSkipped` until Phase 2 — depends on BYOK preservation |

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test packages/keycast_flutter/{lib,test}` — no issues
- [x] `flutter test packages/keycast_flutter/` — 167/167 passing
- [x] `flutter test test/services/pending_verification_service_test.dart test/screens/auth/secure_account_screen_test.dart test/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit_test.dart` — 38/38 passing
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/divine_auth/` — 64/64 passing (regression-safety on the path that never carried nsec)
- [x] `bash mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` — exits 0 on this branch
- [x] Guard regex verified: matches `body['nsec']` + `'nsec':`; ignores `containsKey('nsec')` + `any(named: 'nsec')`
- [ ] Manual: e2e secure-account upgrade flow on a local dev stack (post-merge or staging)
- [ ] Coordinate with infra/security on retention review for any pre-fix request bodies that infra-layer components may have captured (separate workstream)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

title: chore(comments): l10n, design-system, and code-style cleanup
body:
## Context

PR #4618 split `CommentsBloc` into three focused blocs. The refactor is architecturally clean, but several pre-existing l10n and design-system gaps in the comments UI files were surfaced during review. Filing separately so they don't block the refactor.

All items are in files under `lib/screens/comments/` and the new bloc files.

---

## Important

### I1. `_ErrorState` in `comments_list.dart` — hardcoded English + raw `TextStyle`

`'Failed to load comments'` is hardcoded when `commentsErrorLoadFailed` already exists in the ARB. Also uses raw `TextStyle(color: VineTheme.error)` instead of `VineTheme.*Font()`.

### I2. `_CommentsTitle` — hardcoded plural logic

```dart
'$count ${count == 1 ? 'Comment' : 'Comments'}'
```

Should use ICU plural syntax in an ARB key and `context.l10n.commentsHeaderCount(count)`.

### I3. `_CommentsSortToggle` — 4 hardcoded English strings

`'New'`, `'Top'`, `'Old'`, `'Comments sorting'` (semantic label). User-facing text and accessibility labels.

### I4. `comment_item.dart` — 6 hardcoded English strings

`'Reply'`, `'Reply to comment'`, `'Remove upvote'`, `'Upvote comment'`, `'Remove downvote'`, `'Downvote comment'`. These are accessibility labels that screen readers announce.

### I5. Section-header divider comments

`// --- Cross-bloc store mutations ---` and similar in `comments_list_bloc.dart` and `comments_list_event.dart`. Violates `code_style.md`.

### I6. Public mocks in test files

`MockCommentsListBloc`, `MockCommentComposerBloc`, `MockCommentReactionsBloc` in `comments_screen_test.dart` and `comments_list_test.dart` should be `_Mock*` per `testing.md`.

### I7. Hardcoded English strings in test assertions

`comments_list_test.dart` and `comments_screen_test.dart` assert on hardcoded strings like `'Failed to load comments'`, `'5 Comments'`, `'No comments yet'`, `'Get the party started!'`. Should use `lookupAppLocalizations(const Locale('en'))`.

---

## Nits

- **N1.** `GoogleFonts.bricolageGrotesque(...)` in `_CommentsTitle` — should use `VineTheme.*Font()`.
- **N2.** 3 raw `TextStyle(...)` in `comment_item.dart` — should use `VineTheme.*Font()`.
- **N3.** 3 raw `SvgPicture.asset(DivineIconName.*.assetPath)` in `comment_item.dart` — should use `DivineIcon`.
- **N4.** 3 raw `Icons.*` in `_CommentsSortToggle` — should use `DivineIcon`.
- **N5.** `OutboxBridges._idSetsEqual` allocates two `Set`s before checking length — could short-circuit on `.keys.length` first.
- **N6.** `_restoreOriginalCommentAfterFailedEdit` creates a new Nostr event ID orphaning replies — needs inline comment documenting the constraint.
- **N7.** `_toSuggestion` in `CommentComposerBloc` uses no instance state — should be `static`.
- **N8.** `CommentNode` in `comments_list_state.dart` missing `@immutable`.
- **N9.** ABOUTME header comments in the 3 new bloc files duplicate the `///` doc comments below them.

title: feat(dm): basic markdown formatting support (bold, italic, etc.) (#4621)
body:
## Description

Adds inline markdown rendering and a compose-side selection toolbar to DM messages, matching what users expect from WhatsApp / Telegram / Signal / Slack. The wire format stays untouched — NIP-17 `kind 14` content is still plain text, so non-Divine Nostr clients see readable markdown source.

**Supported inline syntax (this PR):**

| Syntax | Result |
|---|---|
| `**bold**` | **bold** |
| `_italic_` | *italic* |
| `~~strikethrough~~` | ~~strikethrough~~ |
| `` `code` `` | `code` with a translucent monospace chip |
| `[label](url)` | tappable `label`, opens URL with the same external-link confirm sheet plain URLs already use |

**What's new in compose:** when the user has a non-empty selection in the DM composer, the system text-selection toolbar gains four prepended actions — **Bold / Italic / Strikethrough / Code** — each of which wraps the selection with the corresponding markdown delimiter. Re-tapping the same action on a selection that's already wrapped unwraps it. Toolbar state changes flow through `EditableTextState.userUpdateTextEditingValue(..., SelectionChangedCause.toolbar)` so the platform's undo/redo stack tracks edits cleanly.

**Architecture (zero blast radius on linkified text):** a new `mobile/lib/widgets/markdown/` module ships a small hand-rolled inline parser (`InlineMarkdownParser` + sealed AST) and a `MarkdownTextSpanBuilder` that walks the AST into `List<InlineSpan>`. Plain leaves are *delegated* back into the existing `LinkifiedTextSpanBuilder`, so URLs / @mentions / #hashtags / nostr refs keep their tap recognizers inside markdown wraps (e.g. `**check @alice**` renders bold *and* keeps `@alice` tappable). `LinkifiedText` and its ~20 other call sites (comments, profile bios, video descriptions, …) are not modified.

The parser uses a CommonMark left/right-flanking word-boundary rule for `_italic_` so `snake_case_identifiers` stay literal, applies a recursion-depth cap of 8 so pathological input can't blow the stack, and falls through to literal characters on any unclosed / empty / malformed delimiter — no throws.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4621

## Out of Scope

- Block markdown (headings, lists, quotes, fenced code blocks, tables, images, footnotes) — per the issue's explicit scope.
- Single-`*` italic / single-`~` strikethrough (collides with arithmetic and casual prose).
- Translations for the four new ARB keys (`dmFormatBold`, `dmFormatItalic`, `dmFormatStrikethrough`, `dmFormatCode`) — added to `_knownUntranslatedDebt` until the next l10n pass picks them up.
- Markdown rendering in comments / profile bios / video descriptions — the parser + builder are reusable, but only the DM bubble opts in this PR.
- Multi-line composer (tracked separately in #4620) — markdown parsing is line-agnostic, so it'll activate automatically there once #4620 lands.

title: fix(auth): require explicit confirmation before cross-account session recovery
body:
## Description

After a non-destructive sign-out with two accounts on device, `_redirectRecoveryToRemainingAccount` would stamp account B's npub as `last_used_npub` and place B's OAuth session in the global slot. On the next cold start — whether the session was still valid or had expired and been refreshed — the app would silently complete sign-in as B even though the user's active session belonged to account A. Users saw this as their local drafts and clips suddenly disappearing.

The fix introduces a session-recovery anchor (`session_recovery_anchor_npub`) written by `signOut()` on non-destructive sign-outs. The cold-start restore path in `_restoreDivineRpcOrFallbackUnauthenticated` checks this anchor against the candidate session's pubkey (for both the direct-restore and post-refresh paths) and blocks the auto sign-in when they differ, routing to unauthenticated instead. The welcome screen reads the anchor, pre-selects the correct account, and shows a contextual banner explaining draft ownership when a different account is highlighted.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4624

## Out of Scope

Full redesign of the returning-user layout to show both accounts side-by-side. The minimal banner approach is sufficient for the fix.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze` — no issues
- `dart format` — no changes

title: Bug: require explicit confirmation before session recovery lands in a different saved account
body:
## Summary
The app has account-pinned restore paths, but the Divine OAuth re-login path can still complete under a different saved account than the one the user was just using. When that happens, the user experiences their local drafts and clips as suddenly missing.

## Incident evidence
- The user was actively publishing as pubkey `c4a39f1291291d452405cd8ddd798c4a29a3858c52cd0d843f1f6852cf17682e`.
- After the logout/re-login path, the restored session belonged to `fc7031a810ce4b02b6195a7e477cfe3d08c0386038bd45b4431f82d9b3f5ffb0`.
- The log shows two known accounts present on the device.

## Why this matters
A cross-account restore looks exactly like data loss to the user, even if owner-scoped local data still exists. The app needs to keep session recovery pinned to the active account or ask the user to confirm a different account explicitly.

## Suspected code areas
- `mobile/lib/services/auth_service.dart` `signInForAccount()` for Divine OAuth restore
- `mobile/lib/services/auth_service.dart` `signInWithDivineOAuth()` integration path
- welcome/account-selection flows in `mobile/lib/blocs/welcome/welcome_bloc.dart`

## Fix direction
- When recovering from an active signed-in session, require the same pubkey by default.
- If the recovered session resolves to a different pubkey, show a confirmation screen before completing the switch.
- Surface which account owns the currently hidden drafts/clips and offer a clear switch-back path.

## Acceptance criteria
- Expired-session recovery defaults to the previously active account.
- A different-account restore requires explicit user confirmation.
- If the user chooses the other account, the UI clearly explains that local drafts/clips belong to a different account.
- Add regression coverage for two saved accounts plus expired-session recovery.

title: Epic: harden account switching and session recovery for local drafts, clips, and publish flows
body:
## Summary
A user on iPhone running 1.0.14+723 reported that the app logged them out while publishing a clip. After logging back in, their drafts folder and clips library appeared empty.

The attached log export shows the clip post itself published successfully, but the app then routed into login/session recovery and re-authenticated into a different account. That identity change caused the prior account's owner-scoped local content to disappear from view and may also have triggered destructive cleanup for the prior account.

This epic tracks the account-switching/session-recovery correctness work needed so local creator data survives auth transitions and users do not silently land in the wrong account.

## User impact
- In-progress publish flows can be interrupted by auth/session recovery.
- Users can appear to "lose" drafts and saved clips after re-login.
- A cross-account re-auth can be mistaken for data loss.
- Current cleanup behavior may actually delete prior-account local rows.

## Evidence from the reported incident
- Publish completed successfully at 2026-05-22 08:02:17.
- The published event was sent under pubkey `c4a39f1291291d452405cd8ddd798c4a29a3858c52cd0d843f1f6852cf17682e`.
- Session recovery/login flow was entered around 2026-05-22 08:02:09.
- Re-auth completed under pubkey `fc7031a810ce4b02b6195a7e477cfe3d08c0386038bd45b4431f82d9b3f5ffb0`.
- `_setupUserSession` then detected an identity change and ran destructive cleanup for the old pubkey.

## Scope
- Make expired-session recovery preserve the active flow until refresh definitively fails.
- Ensure account recovery stays pinned to the intended account unless the user explicitly confirms a switch.
- Preserve owner-scoped drafts, clips, and pending uploads across non-destructive account changes.
- Add coverage for publish + session-expiry + re-auth/account-switch edge cases.

## Child issues
- [ ] #4626 Bug: keep publish flow alive while expired-session recovery is in progress on iOS
- [ ] #4625 Bug: preserve owner-scoped drafts, clips, and uploads across non-destructive account changes
- [ ] #4624 Bug: require explicit confirmation before session recovery lands in a different saved account

## Acceptance criteria
- Expired session recovery does not unnecessarily eject the user from an active publish flow.
- Re-auth does not silently restore a different saved account without explicit confirmation.
- Owner-scoped drafts/clips/uploads survive non-destructive account switching and are visible again when the user returns to that account.
- Regression tests cover the reported path on iOS-oriented auth/publish flows.

title: Bug: keep publish flow alive while expired-session recovery is in progress on iOS
body:
## Summary
On iPhone, an expired Divine OAuth session can interrupt an in-progress publish flow and route the user into login/session recovery before silent refresh has definitively failed.

In the reported incident, the clip upload and publish succeeded, but the app still routed into `/welcome/login-options` during session recovery. That makes the app feel like it logged the user out mid-publish.

## Incident evidence
- Silent refresh attempt starts at `2026-05-22 08:02:09` (`tryRefreshExpiredSession: attempting silent refresh`).
- Router redirects to `/welcome/login-options` at the same time, while auth state is still reported as authenticated.
- Publish later completes successfully at `2026-05-22 08:02:17`.

## Why this matters
Even when the publish succeeds, the user experiences the flow as a forced logout during creation. If refresh fails for real, the app still needs to preserve enough local state for a clean resume.

## Suspected code areas
- `mobile/lib/services/auth_service.dart` around `tryRefreshExpiredSession()` and `_tryRefreshOAuthSession()`
- `mobile/lib/screens/settings/settings_screen.dart` session-expired handling
- `mobile/lib/widgets/profile/profile_header_widget.dart` session-expired handling
- Router/auth redirect interactions during refresh

## Fix direction
- Treat silent refresh as atomic from the UI's perspective.
- Do not navigate away from the active flow until refresh definitively fails.
- Preserve publish state while refresh is in flight.
- If refresh fails, resume from a durable interrupted-publish state after re-auth.

## Acceptance criteria
- Successful silent refresh keeps the user in the active publish flow.
- Failed silent refresh surfaces a resumable interrupted-publish path instead of losing local context.
- Add regression coverage for publish + app resume + expired session on iOS-oriented flows.

title: Bug: preserve owner-scoped drafts, clips, and uploads across non-destructive account changes
body:
## Summary
When `_setupUserSession` detects an identity change, the current cleanup path can delete owner-scoped local rows for the previous pubkey. That is too destructive for account switching and mismatched re-login recovery.

Drafts, clips, and pending uploads are already owner-scoped. In non-destructive account transitions they should become hidden from the current account, not deleted.

## Incident evidence
- The reported publish flow ran under pubkey `c4a39f1291291d452405cd8ddd798c4a29a3858c52cd0d843f1f6852cf17682e`.
- Re-auth completed under pubkey `fc7031a810ce4b02b6195a7e477cfe3d08c0386038bd45b4431f82d9b3f5ffb0`.
- `_setupUserSession` logged `identity change detected` and invoked cleanup for the old pubkey with `deleteUserData: true`.
- That cleanup path deletes drafts, clips, and pending uploads for the old user.

## Suspected code areas
- `mobile/lib/services/auth_service.dart` identity-change handling in `_setupUserSession()`
- `mobile/lib/providers/social_providers.dart` `UserDataCleanupService.onDatabaseCleanup` callback
- owner-scoped local storage/query paths in `DraftStorageService` and `ClipLibraryService`

## Why this matters
This turns an account switch or cross-account restore into apparent data loss. It also risks real deletion of local creator work that should still exist when the user switches back to the original account.

## Fix direction
- Reserve destructive per-user DAO deletion for explicit account removal / delete-keys flows only.
- On ordinary identity change, clear only truly global caches and keep owner-scoped local content intact.
- Audit pending uploads and any adjacent owner-scoped creator state for the same behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- Switching from account A to account B does not delete account A's drafts, clips, or pending uploads.
- Switching back to account A restores visibility of its local creator data.
- Explicit account removal still performs destructive cleanup for that account.
- Add regression tests covering multi-account local-data preservation.

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Summary

The DM message input field is currently limited to a single line. Long messages get truncated visually and there is no way to compose a multi-paragraph message comfortably. The input should auto-grow vertically as the user types, up to roughly 5 lines, and then become scrollable.

## Current behavior

- The DM composer text field is fixed to one line.
- Typing a longer message scrolls horizontally instead of wrapping, which makes it hard to review what you're about to send.
- No way to insert a line break.

## Proposed behavior

- Text field starts at 1 line.
- As the user types and content wraps, the field auto-grows up to a maximum of ~5 lines.
- Beyond 5 lines, content scrolls vertically inside the field; the field height stays capped so it doesn't push the keyboard / send button off-screen.
- Pressing Return inserts a newline (standard messenger behavior). Send is triggered by the send button.
- Works correctly with the keyboard shown, on both iOS and Android, in portrait and landscape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Composer auto-grows from 1 to 5 lines as content wraps.
- [ ] Beyond 5 lines, content scrolls inside the input; outer layout doesn't jump.
- [ ] Return key inserts a newline; sending is only triggered by the explicit send action.
- [ ] Existing send / attach / emoji affordances stay aligned with the bottom of the (now taller) input.
- [ ] Works with system font scaling (no clipping at large text sizes).
- [ ] Behavior matches the pattern users expect from iMessage / WhatsApp / Signal / Telegram.

## Notes

- Related: markdown formatting support in the DM composer (separate issue).
- This was requested on Discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/1470168817589158040/1470256031434149953/1506329272384753765)
